prompt: Half of visitors, chosen at random, see the new pricing page.
why: Random split comparison is an A/B test.
trap: It's not a fake door; both pages are real.

prompt: The team stopped the test on day two when B looked ahead, and the win vanished later.
tells: stopped the test on day two
why: Peeking and stopping early gives false wins. Fix the sample size first.
trap: The metric wasn't vanity; the test was cut short.

prompt: Sales rose after the redesign, but it was also December, so they ran a proper split test.
tells: so they ran a proper split test
why: Before-and-after mixes in other causes. A/B tests isolate the change.
trap: Seasonality is the confounder; the fix is the test.

prompt: A 0.3% lift on 200 users isn't trusted until there's enough data.
tells: isn't trusted until there's enough data
why: A/B results need enough sample to be real.
trap: It's not vanity; it's statistical noise.

prompt: Version B changes only the button text, so any difference comes from that.
why: One change per test makes the cause clear.
trap: It's small, but it's a test, not an MVP.

prompt: Clicks on the new design spiked for a week, then fell back to normal.
why: Novelty effects fool short A/B tests. Run long enough.
